topStories.headline: Diamond Heights Bank Robbed in Midday Holdup; SFPD Bank Robbery Unit Investigating
topStories.dek: A suspect robbed the Bank of America branch in Diamond Heights on Monday afternoon and fled with cash; no injuries were reported.
topStories.body:
A robbery occurred at the Bank of America branch in Diamond Heights on Monday, August 10, at approximately 2:30 p.m., according to the Glen Park Association. A suspect entered the branch, robbed it, and left with an undisclosed amount of money. No one was injured in the incident.

The San Francisco Police Department has obtained a description of the suspect and has turned the investigation over to the SFPD Bank Robbery Unit. As of press time, no arrests had been announced.

Residents with information about the incident are encouraged to contact SFPD at 1-415-575-4444 or submit a tip by texting TIP411 and beginning the message with 'SFPD.' The Diamond Heights Bank of America is located in the Diamond Heights Shopping Center, which serves as a commercial hub for the hilltop neighborhood.

topStories.headline: Grand Lake Kitchen's Noe Valley Outpost Is Drawing Rave Reviews Four Months In
topStories.dek: The East Bay comfort-food institution's first San Francisco location, at the former Mr. Digby's space on Church Street, has quickly become a neighborhood staple.
topStories.body:
Grand Lake Kitchen, the Oakland-born comfort-food restaurant known for its upscale diner-style dishes, has settled firmly into Noe Valley four months after opening its first San Francisco location. Mission Local revisited the spot this week and found it as busy and celebratory as ever, with the refurbished space at 1199 Church Street — formerly Mr. Digby's Bar, and before that Noe's Cantina — drawing a loyal crowd.

The restaurant soft-opened in mid-March 2026 and moved to seven-days-a-week service in April. Co-owners May Seto Wasem and Dave Wasem, who also run two Oakland locations, conceived the Noe Valley spot as a neighborhood bistro serving brunch and dinner with a full bar and patio.

The menu leans into nostalgic comfort dishes executed with care: smoked trout toast, fried green tomatoes with pimento cheese, and a Dungeness crab sandwich on sourdough have earned early fans. Mission Local's reviewer, who visited twice, found the space bustling and the kitchen consistent.

The opening reflects a broader trend of well-regarded East Bay restaurants expanding across the Bay into San Francisco's sunnier southern neighborhoods.

topStories.headline: BART's New Schedule, Longer Trains Now in Effect at Glen Park Station
topStories.dek: A systemwide BART schedule overhaul that took effect August 10 brings longer peak-hour trains and improved headways to riders at the Glen Park station.
topStories.body:
Riders boarding at Glen Park BART station are now operating under a new systemwide schedule that took effect Monday, August 10, 2026. The change, announced by BART in July, brings longer trains, more evenly spaced departures, and targeted improvements designed to reduce delays and platform crowding across the network.

For the Red Line, peak-period trains now run as 10-car trains — up from 8- and 6-car configurations — while off-peak service uses 5-car trains. BART described the August 10 package as a permanent schedule rewrite rather than a one-time maintenance adjustment.

The changes were coordinated through what transit agencies are calling 'The Big Sync,' a regional initiative in which BART, Caltrain, and other Bay Area transit operators aligned their schedule-change windows to twice a year — mid-August and mid-January — to make transfers more reliable. Agencies met in February 2026 to identify opportunities to improve connections.

Glen Park commuters are advised to check the BART Trip Planner at bart.gov, as some individual departure times have shifted by several minutes. Late-evening service between Daly City and Millbrae continues to see delays Sunday through Thursday after 9 p.m. due to ongoing construction to replace BART's train-control system.

events.title: Glen Park Night Market

events.description: The third-Saturday summer night market returns to Kern Street with local artists, artisan vendors, live music, DJ sets, and a family-friendly kids zone with face-painting and activities. Free admission; presented by the Glen Park Association, Glen Park Merchants Association, and Art Walk SF.

events.description: The regular Sunday morning market at Noe Valley's beloved town square features local vendors and a community gathering atmosphere. Free to attend.

events.title: Castro Night Market

Free and open to the public; presented by CG Events, the Castro Merchants Association, and the Civic Joy Fund.

events.title: The Breeders at The Castro Theatre

events.description: Alternative rock icons The Breeders — Kim Deal, Kelley Deal, Josephine Wiggs, and Jim Macpherson — perform at the newly renovated Castro Theatre. The Saturday show is listed as sold out; a second night is scheduled for Sunday, August 23.

events.title: Carnival Family Block Party at the Castro
events.description: The Castro Merchants Association hosts a free, family-friendly Carnival block party featuring LGBTQ+ artists, live music, and drag performances in the heart of the Castro. No ticket required.

moreNews.headline: Castro Theatre Thriving Six Months After Landmark Reopening
moreNews.body: The Castro Theatre, which reopened February 6, 2026 after a $41 million renovation by Another Planet Entertainment, is now a firmly established live-event venue drawing acts from across the music and comedy world. The two-year renovation updated everything from seating to plumbing while preserving the 1922 building's ornate interior designed by architect Timothy Pfleuger. APE projects the venue will draw more than 200,000 visitors annually, and its 2026 calendar — featuring acts including Lucy Dacus, Santigold, and The Breeders — has bolstered foot traffic for neighboring Castro businesses.

moreNews.headline: Castro Upper Market Entertainment Zone Now Operational, Boosting Night Market Sales
moreNews.body: The Castro Upper Market Entertainment Zone — the fourth such zone established in San Francisco — is now fully operational, allowing bars and restaurants along 18th Street, Castro Street, and portions of Market and Church streets to sell alcoholic beverages in compostable or reusable to-go containers during approved special events. The zone was approved unanimously by the SF Board of Supervisors and launched officially at the Castro Night Market earlier this year. Mayor Daniel Lurie signed companion legislation in May 2026 creating five additional entertainment zones citywide, signaling broad city support for the program.

moreNews.headline: Glen Park Night Markets Draw Over 1,000 Attendees per Event in Second Summer Season
moreNews.body: The Glen Park Night Markets are back for their second summer, running every third Saturday from June through September on Kern Street between Diamond and Brompton streets. The series, funded by a grant from the Civic Joy Fund and presented by the Glen Park Association and Glen Park Merchants Association, features local artisans, live music, DJ sets, food vendors, and a children's activity zone. The next market is Saturday, August 15, from 4 to 8:30 p.m.
